description: Draft contracts this build can read ONLY through the explicitly requested rule-V7 lane. These are not released contracts: neither type has a row in the shared schemas/versions.json, a published schemaVersion of its own, a w3id URL or a release tag, and nothing in this file changes that. Each entry pins the exact bytes of one draft file by the commit of the development repository that owns the type and the SHA-256 of those bytes, which is how docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md V7 requires a draft to be read: selection runs against the pinned bytes, never against a repository's main at run time. Two revisions are pinned per type and they are different things: `commit` is the revision of the contract bytes this library compiles and validates against, and `suiteCommit` is the revision of the owning repository's development conformance suite whose manifest `scripts/draft_vectors.jl` executes. They are separate keys because the two files move at different times, and because the suite carries the rule labels this file quotes: a claim about C1/C2/C3 or K1-K6 is a claim about the suite revision, never about the contract revision. Where they are equal, `suiteCommit` repeats `commit` so the check is uniform. `src/drafts.jl` re-verifies every digest the first time a draft is loaded and refuses to read on a mismatch; `test/runtests.jl` calls `verify_draft_bytes()` on every test run, and `check_suite_pin()` is the guard the draft runner refuses to score without. The lane is never the default: with no explicit user decision these files are not read at all and a draft citation is 'any other value' under V5, exactly as it was before the lane existed. This registry is deliberately separate from schemas/provenance.json, which lists released contracts only and stays that way.
rule: docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md rule V7 (FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification#221/#226, text published at tag v0.6.0)

scheduledPublication.note: A scheduled future release is a decision about that type, not a licence to publish it here. Until the release lands these entries stay drafts: no schemaVersion claim, no fixed alias, no registry row, no support claim.

FHT.verification: Re-measured on 2026-11-15 at this re-pin (the original 2026-11-15 pin above it measured suite 24d3b033 / manifest 9b071794 / 56250 B / 66 vectors; the upstream suite has since grown six vectors). Bytes were read through the GitHub contents API at immutable full-commit refs and hashed locally, never through a mutable branch name: fht.json at 226f923c28b680edb3c546e99a751482d06aef1a is 29430 bytes, sha256 59ad9641adcb0e5591045c2d894c066d1adc9984cca84c5ff6502f8dad88487e - unchanged, so the contract pin does not move - and live main (09dafdf8182c84c3689bd5efeeafcdb7a803a443) publishes byte-identical content, `cmp` clean against the vendored file; the suite manifest at 09dafdf8182c84c3689bd5efeeafcdb7a803a443 (conformance/manifest.json) is 65615 bytes, sha256 9fd8c0b2a4638d5ddc0bf9b5d1e96c66778b26bcf8f93975aafb707d8f2b702c, and it lists 72 vectors: the 66 already covered plus fht-fasta-gzip-multimember, fht-fasta-gzip-sequence-tampered, fht-fasta-parent-subset-citing-whole, fht-fasta-parent-masked-exact, fht-fasta-parent-real-digest-wrong-file and fht-fasta-parent-case-folded-digest (adding rule coverage at R1, R3 and C3; no vector was removed). A separate `git clone` checkout at the same commit digests identically, so the API and the git object store agree.
FHT.note: An FHT header is a FASTA `;~` block like FHR, so it shares the FASTA container; the type is decided by the record's own `schema` citation. Its conformance rules are C1 (contract validation), C2 (schema-URL closure) and C3 (parent-link verification) - text in the FHT-Specification conformance README. C2 is inside the pinned bytes; C3 is judged by the draft-lane runner in scripts/draft_vectors.jl, which recomputes a supplied parent's checksum and reports checked-pass / checked-fail / unchecked per derivedFrom entry. C3 is not claimed for the released types.

FHGM.verification: Re-measured on 2026-11-15 at this re-pin through the GitHub contents API at immutable full-commit refs, hashed locally. The RECORD CONTRACT has not moved: its bytes were already bf1553cac04dc88d8afaff1d39bc50360342e1ebedac4b73dfe3dff570ff410f (9564 B) at the previous pin ac3d37b3033312844fc3151217731928ae33aa54 and are byte-identical at the new one (`cmp` clean against the vendored file), so the contract's digest claim is unchanged. What moved is the TRANSPORT OVERLAY (see transportOverlay below: 1363 B dd9f6927 -> 2613 B d1619cce at commit 5d15ccc122fcb8239787393010364a818a774ee4), and because one contract checkout must satisfy both contract-side pins, `commit` advances to a revision whose tree carries both pinned byte sets - it is set to the live main measured here, c503ecf38deaba289e8384124ee5e2b8e81b86f1; the record contract itself gained nothing at this commit. The suite manifest at that commit (development/conformance/manifest.json) is 51114 bytes, sha256 0d2790151c4a29551e9b92fb6b3c3c62ea062f2889ffbd00b3c425e7b6da3458, and it lists 43 vectors: the 31 previously covered plus twelve D. melanogaster real-data cases (dmel-snapshot-v1, dmel-snapshot-v2-resolved, dmel-duplicate-model-id, dmel-empty-model-array, dmel-numeric-model-version, dmel-pointer-names-neighbor, dmel-pointer-reuses-version, dmel-reference-contradicts-file, dmel-reference-not-comparable, dmel-revision-without-history, dmel-target-absent, dmel-target-transcript-row; the manifest bytes last changed at d443073a6b9d32114fafd9da1d55e5759afc1fc1). The earlier 2026-11-15 measurement that this entry replaces recorded the manifest at ac3d37b3 as 35269 B / 31 vectors, sha256 31f14f022ff0858191170d1c8285bd83c7f943d88fd8cebc70f11712525617db. A nonsense path on the same repository returned HTTP 404 under the freshness job's control probe, and that advisory job then confirmed all five pinned targets match the live raw-main bytes, so the pin is current as measured and the 200s are not a soft-200 portal artefact. A separate `git clone` checkout at the same commit digests identically, so the API and the git object store agree. Note this history: the manifest moved 35269 B -> 36001 B (sha256 5620f00cbb4bcb4bb3344220c3a20407c38de78ca50bf1010f56977311985551, at 5d15ccc1, vector count still 31 - a digest-only move that a count-only check cannot see) -> 51114 B (at d443073a, count 31 -> 43); which is why the guard digests first and counts second.

transportOverlay.note: Transport-only overlay: since the upstream maintainer decision of 2026-11-15 (FHGM-Specification PR #17, byte change at 5d15ccc1) it admits EITHER released FHGFF3 file identity a carrier can cite today - the v0.5.0 citation with schemaVersion "1.1", or the v0.6.0 citation with schemaVersion "1.2" - as two CLOSED branches pairing each schema-URI set with its version, so a citation and a stated version that contradict each other are rejected rather than falling back to a single pin; 1.0 stays inadmissible. It still requires a non-empty `x-fhgm-models` array and says nothing about record contents: those are the model contract above. src/fhgm.jl applies K1 from the published extension rule (docs/FORMAT.md R15: extension fields are admitted from FHGFF3 1.1, so a 1.2 header qualifies too) and offers `overlay = true` to apply the pinned overlay's closed-branch pairing instead, which is what the upstream FHGM checker does. The previous overlay (1363 B, sha256 dd9f69274f26860bbfd71d0e8b2794420c5369fb5d40ce838fb6a9e6d5116e3d at ac3d37b3) pinned only the v0.5.0/1.1 branch; that is why a re-pin changes bytes, not just labels.

FHGM.note: FHGM is not a file header type: an FHGM record carries no `schema`, no `schemaVersion` and no `checksum`. Records ride inside an FHGFF3 header under the R15 extension key `x-fhgm-models`, the file keeps its released FHGFF3 citation and is routed by V1 to V3, and the file checksum covers every record byte (R3). The V7 lane therefore selects only the contract applied to the records; a file citing the FHGM contract URL as its `schema` is 'any other value' under V5, with the lane open or shut. Model-level rules K1-K6 and the boundary B1 are drafted in FHGM-Specification; src/fhgm.jl implements K1, K2, K3, K5 and K6 and reports K4 (feature-target resolution) as not-supported-yet, because resolving a featureId needs the GFF3 feature layer, which this library's boundary assigns to gff3-validator.
